notes:
Account snapshot: Helix is an enterprise IoT analytics vendor (telemetry ingestion from edge devices, real-time anomaly scores, customer-facing chat ops + internal assistant). Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable high-throughput model serving across NA + EU regions.

Primary ask (summary):
- Reserved GPU pool planning: need a design that supports primary NA region (us-east) + failover to eu-west with <500ms extra failover latency for chat sessions.
- Throughput guarantees: sustained 1.2k concurrent chat sessions with 16-token/sec per session average token emission => planning baseline 4x concurrency headroom.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms for short-turn chat (<=256 tokens), p95 <= 250ms for long-turns (<=1024 tokens).
- Failover headroom: plan for 25% spare capacity in each region to absorb zone failures and sudden traffic spikes; prefer cross-region burst policy with automated warm standby.
- Model footprint: ensemble of gpt-style open models (Llama-2-70B local quantized variant, a trimmed 30B variant for fallback). Will require mixed precision + int8 quantization support.
- Routing: traffic routed by policy - latency-first to local pool, cost-fallback to trimmed variant, emergency fallback to hosted API for degraded zones.
- Security/compliance: VPC-only control plane for private deployment, KMS-integration for keys, retention controls for PII, audit logs forwarded to Helix SIEM.

Recent timeline / activities (bullets pulled from AE notes):
- 2026-02-10: Intro demo (Maya + Ravi) — high-level dedicated pitch; customer extremely latency-sensitive. Asked for POC sizing.
- 2026-02-18: Security touchpoint with Helix infosec — provided SOC2 artifacts + draft network diagram. SE action: sample encryption keyflow.
- 2026-02-25: Fireflies call (ff-20260225-helix) — discussed model variants, quantization tolerance, canaries. Quote: "We need predictable token costs more than occasional peak speed."
- 2026-03-01: Sizing workshop (on-site) — collected 90th/95th percentile token emission profiles, spike traces from edge ingestion, agreed on target baseline 60 GPUs (A100 equivalent) across two regions for POC. SE noted need to validate inter-region replication latency.
- 2026-03-04: Internal cost model shared (drive link) — Helix highlighted sensitivity to sustained per-token cost. Interested in Optimizer recommendations (batching + cache profiles).
- 2026-03-06: Legal/Procurement pre-reqs call — Helix requests SLA items: credit windows, latency SLOs, guaranteed throughput levels, maintenance windows.

POC plan / technical checklist:
- POC scope: 6-week evaluation: 3 weeks perf/load testing on dedicated pool in us-east, 2 weeks cross-region failover test to eu-west, final 1 week for SLA negotiation and runbook handoff.
- Acceptance criteria: demonstrate p95 latency targets at sustained 1.2k concurrent sessions for short-turn and 800 concurrent for long-turn with <10% error rate; automated failover <30s for active sessions and <500ms median additional token latency post-failover for new sessions.
- Reserved capacity design proposal (drafted by SE):
  * us-east primary pool: 40 GPUs (A100 eq), 25% hot spare -> 50 GPUs logical for headroom and burst.
  * eu-west standby pool: 20 GPUs reserved, with on-demand burst allowance of +10 GPUs via cross-region borrowing for 48 hrs.
  * AZ spread: minimum 3 AZs per region, with autoscale disabled for the reserved baseline; burst policy triggers limited autoscale on demand.
  * KV/prefix cache replication: deploy regional cache with async replication; warm-up strategy for model KV cache during failover.
  * Canary routing: 5% traffic shift for new model variants, automated rollback on quality regressions.

SLA negotiation points flagged by Helix:
- Guaranteed throughput units and measurable metrics (tokens/sec consumed per GPU, baseline vs burst).
- Downtime windows: preferred maintenance window windows and credit multipliers for exceeded SLOs.
- RPO/RTO for metadata and KV caches during regional failover.
- Data residency clauses for EU traffic and audit log retention periods.

Cost / commercial notes:
- Helix is pricing-sensitive: total ARR target mid-range $250k–$1M. Prefers 12-month reserved contract with upfront commit discount.
- Will request a dedicated pricing sheet that maps per-GPU reserved tiers to sustained token throughput and expected per-token cost. SE to deliver by 2026-03-12.

Open actions (who / due):
- SE (Ravi): finalize GPU sizing calc and verification plan (due 2026-03-10).
- AE (Maya): coordinate procurement checklist + send draft pricing sheet (due 2026-03-12).
- INF Eng: validate cross-region KV replication latency in staging (ticket INF-2893).
- Security: prepare ISO/SOC2 supplemental artifacts and KMS integration note (ticket SEC-412).

Notes / shorthand and quotes: 
- Helix ops lead: "Our fleet needs a guarantee — throttles are OK, but predictable baseline matters."
- They prefer reserved pool + limited burst over pure autoscale; cost predictability trumps raw elasticity.
- Procurement will require a 30-day legal review once pricing sheet is submitted.

Potential risks:
- Mis-estimating warm cache requirements leading to sustained latency spikes on DR failover.
- Inter-region network egress costs if cross-region burst is used often.
- Complexity of quantized model parity causing unexpected quality regressions on fallback variants.

Recommended Redwood playbook items to move deal:
- Deliver a clear reserved GPU sizing workbook that translates traffic profiles to GPU units and headroom assumptions.
- Provide a runbook template for failover steps and KV cache warm-up scripts.
- Offer a 6-week POC commercial that credits back a portion of committed spend if SLOs not met in acceptance tests.

Next planned touchpoints:
- 2026-03-10: SE delivery (sizing workbook) + internal review.
- 2026-03-15: SLA negotiation call (legal + AE + Helix procurement).
- 2026-03-22: Start of POC deploy (once procurement OK).
